The US housing market is in for a wild ride.

As rates rise to new highs, the average interest rate on a 30Y Mortgage is nearing 7%.

In other words, if you bought a home in 2021 at 3% interest, moving to a new home today would increase your rate by ~400 basis points.

Assuming you buy a $500,000 home with 20% down:

1. Monthly Payment at 3% Interest: $1,686/mo
2. Monthly Payment at 7% Interest: $2,661/mo

That's an increase of almost $1,000/mo, or +58%.

The already stagnant housing market is set to freeze.

A Fed that stopped explaining itself just changed the regime for stocks.

Warsh ended his press conference with zero guidance on rates while three of twelve FOMC members voted to hike now. With no anchor, the S&P 500 posted its worst Fed-day selloff since December 2024, the 10-year yield hit its highest since January 2025, and the VIX jumped above 20.

No forward guidance means a higher uncertainty premium: lower equity multiples, wider single-day swings, and cross-asset correlations creeping back toward the 2022 setup. Markets already price a 65% chance of a September hike, which turns that meeting and Jackson Hole into binary, single-day events for stocks. Bigger swings and lower multiples are the cost of a Fed that makes you guess. $SPX

tweets.text:
Japan keeps firing bigger checks to prop up the yen, and it keeps making new lows. A losing fight, and it lands on you.

The chart says it all. Round after round of intervention, each one bigger, the latest 11.73 trillion yen, and the yen still slid to its weakest since 1986 before this week's bounce back to 157.

Why it fails: the BOJ sits at 1%, the Fed at 3.75%. Money chases the higher yield until that gap closes, and no checkbook out-muscles a 2.75-point spread.

The tell: if Japan defends alone, it sells US Treasuries to fund it, and that pushes American yields and mortgage rates up. Japan's currency problem becomes your borrowing problem.

Hedge funds are loading up on oil, and it is a warning for the whole tape.

They added bullish WTI bets at the fastest pace since March, net longs up 21,402 lots to 108,307 in a single week. This is real positioning for supply that keeps getting choked from every direction: the Iran war, Houthi attacks on Saudi shipments in the Red Sea, and now tanker attacks on the Black Sea route that carries Kazakhstan's oil.

The chain: oil up feeds inflation, inflation keeps yields up, and higher yields keep the Fed from cutting. Long-duration tech sits last in line and takes the hardest hit when the discount rate stays pinned.

Energy is the one place positioning and the macro agree. That is where you want to be while oil does the Fed's tightening for it.

tweets.text: On this day in 1981, MTV signed on at 12:01 a.m. with a countdown, a rocket launch, and footage of the Apollo 11 moon landing, as a voice announced, "Ladies and gentlemen, rock and roll." The first video it ever played was "Video Killed the Radio Star." Record executives thought the whole idea was a joke. Why give music away on television when the business ran on selling records and buying radio play? The joke did not last. Labels learned that a single video could break an unknown act nationwide in a weekend, and an industry that had never spent a dollar on film started pouring fortunes into three-minute productions. MTV turned the music video into the most powerful advertisement ever built and wrote the playbook every brand and influencer still runs today. The recorded music business it reshaped is worth $31.7 billion a year. Here are the first 2 hours.
